title: Building Great Agent Skills: The Missing Manual
talk_summary: Matt Pocock gives a rubric for writing agent skills: decide user- vs model-invocation (context load vs cognitive load), split skills into steps + reference, keep skill.md tiny by hiding branch-specific reference behind context pointers, steer with 'leading words' and by splitting steps to force legwork, and prune duplication/sediment/no-ops.

takeaways.technique: User-invoked vs model-invoked skills to control context load
takeaways.what_they_do: Only model-invocable skills put their description in the agent's context on every request; user-invoked skills (disable model invocation) keep the pointer out of context, trading agent context load for human cognitive load and removing invocation unpredictability.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every time you add a model invoked skill into your agent's environment, it increases what I'm going to call the context load on that agent
takeaways.numbers: 100 model-invoked skills = 100 descriptions in context per request

takeaways.technique: Steps + reference split with branch-specific reference behind context pointers
takeaways.what_they_do: Compose each skill from a short step list plus reference material; move reference used only on some branches into separate bundled markdown files pointed to by a context pointer, keeping skill.md minimal.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Hide branching reference material behind context pointers.

takeaways.what_they_do: Embed compact high-meaning phrases (e.g. 'vertical slice') in the skill so the model repeats them in reasoning traces, biasing behavior; verify by watching traces for the phrase.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you put the leading word in the skill itself in the text, and then the agent will repeat the leading word back to itself

takeaways.technique: Split steps into separate skills to force legwork
takeaways.what_they_do: When an agent under-invests in an early step (e.g. clarifying questions before planning), hide the future goal by making that step its own skill so the agent only sees the current phase.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we have step one and step two, but the agent only sees one step at a time

takeaways.technique: Pruning pass: duplication, sediment, no-ops, deletion test
takeaways.what_they_do: Treat oversized skills as a symptom; enforce single source of truth, remove stale accreted content, and delete paragraphs that don't change behavior (deletion test).
takeaways.evidence_quote: things inside the skill that appear to do something but don't actually influence the agent's behavior

takeaways.technique: Use the 'writing great skills' rubric as a lint for agent instructions
takeaways.what_they_do: Provides a checklist (trigger, structure, steering, pruning) that can be run over any skill to judge quality; speaker suggests running it over community skills.
takeaways.evidence_quote: use it to run over some community authored skills so you can check that the skills that you're actually pulling in are any good
